Subject: QBR follow-up: commitments and timeline clarifications

Thanks again for the sync this morning. A couple of quick asks from our execs as we finalize the QBR pack:

1) Can you confirm which features will be in the May pilot vs June GA? Execs want to label any items that are "at risk" for GA.
2) We need an explicit fallback plan if dedicated capacity isn't available for our initial rollout window (June 14-21). What does that look like from Redwood's side?
3) For pricing: we asked for a short note on whether the dedicated discount is negotiable if we commit to 12-month reserved capacity.

I've attached the updated scope table that includes our priority buckets — it might help map to your internal roadmap. Please send a consolidated list of commitments + owners by end of day Friday so we can lock the QBR slide.

Attachment: acme-updates-scope.xlsx

— Hanna

Director, Platform Partnerships | Acme Corp

Subject: Re: QBR follow-up: commitments and timeline clarifications

Hanna — thanks for this and for the scope doc. Short answers up top, then assigned owners and open risks below.

Quick answers:
- May pilot: low-risk items (prefix caching improvements + API surface parity) — owner: Ben Carter.
- June GA: feature set that requires dedicated capacity (KV cache persistence, autoscaling tweaks). These are marked as "targeted GA" but are dependent on capacity confirmation — owner: Vivek.
- Fallback if dedicated capacity not available: we'll support a dual-path rollout: 1) hosted with throttled SLA + prefix caching enabled, 2) targeted subset rollout for initial customers. Full fallback plan below.
- Pricing note: Rishi is evaluating whether a 12-month commit materially changes discounting; he will provide a short memo.

Assigned items (please see deadlines):
- Ben Carter — produce final mutual action plan mapping features to releases (due: 2027-04-12 EOD). Attachment: mutual-action-plan.docx
- Vivek Kulkarni — confirm availability of dedicated pools for 14-21 June and list alternatives (due: 2027-04-09 EOD).
- Rishi Malhotra — pricing memo for 12-month reserved capacity & exception process (due: 2027-04-11).
- Marissa Cole (me) — consolidate exec decision log and slide-ready commitments for QBR (due: 2027-04-13).

Open risks / notes:
- Capacity: regional constraints in us-west could push availability >2 weeks. Vivek, flag any constraints early.
- Quality regression risk if we aggressively quantize for cost savings — will need a short eval plan.

I'll follow up with a consolidated tracker tomorrow morning. 

— Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: QBR follow-up: commitments and timeline clarifications

Quick infra check-in:
- us-west dedicated pool: nominal availability looks tight for the 14-21 June window due to GPU maintenance windows. I can route Acme to a mixed strategy:
  * Option A: reserve a minimal dedicated pool in us-west (best-effort) + staged GA for 2-3 customers (risk: capacity may be preempted).
  * Option B: host initial launch on Redwood hosted API w/ explicit throttling and prefix caching, then switch to dedicated when capacity is confirmed (risk: potential higher token costs for Acme).

I recommend Option B for predictability; it provides a clean fallback and avoids partial GA for only a subset of customers. If Acme is comfortable with a slight cost delta early, we can preserve customer experience. I'll confirm capacity by EOD and include potential blackout dates.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Infra & Dedicated Services | Redwood Inference
